title: Session claim
description: `<root>/.claude/exchange/sessions/<session_id>.json`. One file per session, never a shared append target: concurrent writers on one file is the contention this layout exists to avoid. Seeded at SessionStart from the hook payload, updated by the session through `exchange claim`, removed at SessionEnd. Claims inform and never block - every recorded collision was a read-discipline failure, and a lock on a path would be a new failure mode for no measured benefit. Presence comes from the native registry; this file is the stated intent the registry cannot hold, because the registry's `status` is per-turn and `idle` there means not mid-turn rather than finished.

session_id.description: From the hook payload. Constrained because it is also the filename: anything with a separator in it is rejected rather than resolved.

name.description: The session's own display name, as the native registry knows it.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory. What scope-addressed handoffs are matched against.

git_branch.description: Read from .git/HEAD, not from a subprocess. Absent when detached or outside a repo.

focus.description: What this session is actually doing, in its own words. The one field a machine cannot derive.

repos.description: Root-relative repository directories this session is working in.

paths.description: Hot paths - files or directories being changed. Read this before heavy work in a shared repo.

tickets.description: Opaque references for a human reader. Never parsed.

updated_at.description: UTC, seconds precision, always Z. A claim whose session no longer appears in the native registry is stale regardless of this, which is how a crashed session gets cleaned up without a SessionEnd.
